title: Volume integral scattering and partial wave error

items.title: The three-dimensional volume integral scattering model
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable set, let $M:=|D|$, let $q\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$, and let $k\in\mathbb R$. Here $L^2$ and $L^\infty$ are equivalence classes modulo null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and $L^\infty$ means essentially bounded with respect to Lebesgue measure ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]). We regard $q$ as zero off $D$. The convention is the volume equation
$$u=f+K_k u,\qquad K_k u(x):=\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)u(y)\,dy,\qquad G_k(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|}\quad(z\ne0).$$
Set $G_k(0):=0$; when $M>0$ the diagonal in $D\times D$ is product-null, so this value is only a representative convention. The input and unknown are classes in complex $L^2(D)$, and the displayed equation is interpreted as an equality of those classes. Its formula is well defined by [[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]].

The associated far-field map is
$$\mathcal F_k[v](\theta):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_D e^{-ik\theta\cdot y}q(y)v(y)\,dy,\qquad \theta\in S^2.$$
Here $S^2$ has the surface measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. The map is well defined as a continuous function of $\theta$ by [[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]].

For $x\notin\overline D$, the exterior volume potential is
$$V_kv(x):=\int_D G_k(x-y)q(y)v(y)\,dy.$$
For each $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, the essential-supremum result gives $|q|\le\|q\|_\infty$ almost everywhere, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\|qv\|_{L^1(D)}\le\|q\|_\infty\sqrt M\,\|v\|_2$. Thus, for $x\notin\overline D$, the exterior volume-potential integral is absolutely convergent: $\overline D$ is closed, so its complement contains a ball about $x$ disjoint from $D$.

If $M=0$, define $L^2(D)=\{0\}$ and $K_k=0$; all solution and far-field statements on that space are the zero-space statements. The substantive operator results below assume $0<M<\infty$.

This is a stipulated integral-equation model with the sign convention $(-\Delta-k^2)(u-f)=q u$ when the corresponding distributional Helmholtz equation is used. In the acoustic notation of Scherzer–Mindrinos, their equation $u=u_i-k^2\Phi*((1-n)u)$ corresponds to $q=k^2(n-1)$. No existence or uniqueness for all contrasts is asserted by this definition.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed for the polar surface measure and the well-definedness interfaces. No physical uniqueness claim is part of this definition.

items.title: Rescaling finite-measure kernel operators to probability spaces
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,\mu)$ and $(Y,
u)$ be finite measure spaces with masses $0<M_X:=\mu(X)<\infty$ and $0<M_Y:=
u(Y)<\infty$. Put $d\widehat\mu=d\mu/M_X$ and $d\widehat
u=d
u/M_Y$. For $a\in L^2(X	imes Y,\mu	imes
u)$, let $T_a:L^2(Y,
u)	o L^2(X,\mu)$ be its square-integrable-kernel operator and let $\widehat T$ be the operator with kernel $\widehat a:=\sqrt{M_XM_Y}\,a$ against $\widehat
u$. The maps $U_Xg=\sqrt{M_X}g$ and $U_Yh=\sqrt{M_Y}h$ are unitary and
$$U_XT_aU_Y^{-1}=\widehat T.$$
Moreover $\|\widehat a\|_{L^2(\widehat\mu	imes\widehat
u)}=\|a\|_{L^2(\mu	imes
u)}$, so the operator norms and kernel $L^2$ norms agree. If either mass is zero, the corresponding $L^2$ space and kernel operator are zero.

For $X=Y=D$ with Lebesgue mass $M>0$, the normalized kernel is $\widehat a=Ma$ and the measure is $d\widehat x=dx/M$.
items.axiom_use: AC is carried only to use completed-product kernel operators with the exact well-definedness interface of the published Hilbert–Schmidt supplier; the scaling algebra itself makes no choice.

items.title: Dyadic cell-average projections converge strongly in L2 of a bounded set
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable, and choose a half-open cube $Q$ of positive side length containing $D$. Subdivide $Q$ into its nested dyadic cubes at mesh $h_N=2^{-N}\operatorname{side}(Q)$. Let $E_{N,j}=D\cap Q_{N,j}$ range over the finitely many cells of positive measure, let $V_N\subset L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ be the functions constant on each such cell, and define $P_N$ by replacing a function on each $E_{N,j}$ by its cell average. Then $P_N$ is the orthogonal projection onto $V_N$, $\|P_N\|\le1$, the spaces $V_N$ are increasing, and $P_Nv\to v$ in $L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ for every $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$.
items.axiom_use: Only the hypotheses of the cited dyadic-density result are used; the projection argument uses finite sums and no arbitrary-index choice.

items.title: Spherical harmonics and partial-wave conventions in three dimensions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Use the unit sphere $S^2$ and its polar surface measure $d\sigma$ from [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. For each integer $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the complex vector space of restrictions to $S^2$ of homogeneous degree-$\ell$ polynomials $P$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the Euclidean harmonic equation $\Delta P=0$. For complex-valued polynomials or functions, $\Delta$ and its polar-coordinate formulas act componentwise on real and imaginary parts. In polar coordinates $x=r\omega$, define $\Delta_{S^2}$ by
$$\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}=\partial_r^2+\frac2r\partial_r+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2},$$
equivalently $\Delta_{S^2}=\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta(\sin\theta\partial_\theta)+\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\phi^2$ away from the poles. Thus if $Y\in\mathcal H_\ell$ is the restriction of $P$, then $\Delta_{S^2}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y$.

For $\ell\ge0$, define the normalized zonal polynomial $P_\ell(t)$ to be the degree-$\ell$ polynomial satisfying
$$ (1-t^2)P_\ell''(t)-2tP_\ell'(t)+\ell(\ell+1)P_\ell(t)=0,\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$
The later harmonic-basis lemma proves existence and uniqueness of this normalized polynomial and identifies it with the usual Legendre convention.

The term **partial wave of degree $\ell$** means the $\mathcal H_\ell$ component of an angular expansion in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Completeness, orthogonality, finite dimension, and the evaluation bound for these components are established in [[lem-spherical-harmonics-form-complete-basis-and-addition-formula]].

For a radial field $u(r,\omega)$, its degree-$\ell$ component is written $u_\ell(r,\omega)\in\mathcal H_\ell$; any orthonormal basis within this finite-dimensional space gives the equivalent scalar mode equations. The definition does not select such a basis globally.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed for the polar surface measure and Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for the later normalized-polynomial justification. The definitions make no basis selection.

items.title: The three-dimensional free-space scattering kernel is square integrable
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and Lebesgue measurable, let $M:=|D|$, $d_D:=\operatorname{diam}(D)$, $q\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb C)$, and $k\in\mathbb R$. If $M>0$, define $a(x,y)=G_k(x-y)q(y)$ off the diagonal and set it to zero on the diagonal. Then $a\in L^2(D\times D)$ and
$$\|a\|_{L^2(D\times D)}^2\le\frac{\|q\|_\infty^2 M d_D}{4\pi}.$$
If $M=0$, every measurable kernel on $D\times D$ represents the zero product $L^2$ class.
items.axiom_use: The polar-coordinate and completed-product Tonelli suppliers assume Countable Choice; no full Axiom of Choice is used here.

items.title: The volume far-field map is bounded and is the uniform far-field limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D,q,k$ be as in [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]], with $0<|D|<\infty$, and put $R_0>\sup_{y\in D}|y|$. Then $\mathcal F_k:L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to C(S^2;\mathbb C)$ is linear and
$$\|\mathcal F_kv\|_\infty\le\frac{\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}}{4\pi}\|v\|_2.$$
It is Lipschitz in direction with constant at most $|k|R_0\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}\|v\|_2/(4\pi)$. For every $r\ge2R_0$, the exterior volume potential of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] satisfies
$$\sup_{\theta\in S^2}\left|r e^{-ikr}V_kv(r\theta)-\mathcal F_kv(\theta)\right|\le\frac{2R_0+|k|R_0^2}{4\pi r}\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}\|v\|_2.$$
Thus $\mathcal F_kv$ is the uniform far-field amplitude under the outgoing $e^{ikr}/r$ convention.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed for the surface-measure convention; the pointwise far-field bounds use no further choice.

items.title: Spherical harmonics form a complete basis with the addition formula
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Use $\mathcal H_\ell$ from [[def-spherical-harmonic-partial-wave-conventions]]. For every $\ell\ge0$, $\dim_\mathbb C\mathcal H_\ell=2\ell+1$; the spaces $\mathcal H_\ell$ are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma;\mathbb C)$ and their algebraic sum is dense there. Thus they give a complete orthogonal spherical-harmonic expansion. For any orthonormal basis $Y_{\ell 1},\ldots,Y_{\ell,2\ell+1}$ of $\mathcal H_\ell$, the basis-independent reproducing kernel
$$Z_\ell(\omega,\eta):=\sum_{m=1}^{2\ell+1}Y_{\ell m}(\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\eta)}$$
satisfies $Z_\ell(\omega,\omega)=(2\ell+1)/(4\pi)$. In particular,
$$|g(\omega)|\le\sqrt{\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}}\,\|g\|_{L^2(S^2)}\qquad(g\in\mathcal H_\ell).$$
For fixed $\eta$, rotational invariance makes $Z_\ell(\omega,\eta)$ a degree-$\ell$ zonal polynomial of $\omega\cdot\eta$; normalizing $P_\ell(1)=1$ gives the usual addition identity $Z_\ell(\omega,\eta)=\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}P_\ell(\omega\cdot\eta)$.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are used for regularity and L2 density of the finite surface measure; the finite-dimensional harmonic construction uses no arbitrary-index choice.

items.title: The outgoing three-dimensional Helmholtz kernel is a fundamental solution
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For real $k$, let $\Phi_k(x)=e^{ik|x|}/(4\pi|x|)$ for $x\ne0$. In the sense of distributions on $\mathbb R^3$,
$$(-\Delta-k^2)\Phi_k=\delta_0.$$
Here $\delta_0$ is the point-mass distribution defined by $\langle\delta_0,\varphi\rangle=\varphi(0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$. Consequently, if $g\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ has bounded support, the integral $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Phi_k(x-y)g(y)\,dy$ is absolutely finite for almost every $x$. Define $V$ by this integral almost everywhere (and arbitrarily on the exceptional null set). Then $V\in L^1_{\rm loc}$ and $(-\Delta-k^2)V=g$ distributionally.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is required by the polar-coordinate, second-Green, and locally-integrable-to-distribution interfaces. The point-source identity is a test-function calculation; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: The volume integral operator is well defined and bounded on L2
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ have finite Lebesgue measure. For every product-measurable kernel $a\in L^2(D\times D;\mathbb C)$, the formula $T_av(x)=\int_Da(x,y)v(y)dy$ defines a representative-independent complex-linear map $L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ and $\|T_a\|\le\|a\|_{L^2(D\times D)}$. Consequently, under [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$,
$$\|K_k\|_{L^2\to L^2}\le\|G_k(\cdot-\cdot)q(\cdot)\|_{L^2(D\times D)}\le\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{\frac{|D|\,\operatorname{diam}(D)}{4\pi}}.$$
For $|D|=0$ the operator is zero.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used by the completed-product Tonelli/Fubini interface. No full Axiom of Choice or compactness claim is used in this boundedness branch.

references.title: Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Sommersemester 2015, §5.2.6
references.locator: PDF pp. 79–82, volume-potential definition and its integral equation; this L2 well-definedness estimate is proved locally.

items.title: Exponential coefficient decay gives a uniform partial-wave truncation bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $b_\ell\in\mathcal H_\ell$ for every integer $\ell\ge0$, where $\mathcal H_\ell$ is defined in [[def-spherical-harmonic-partial-wave-conventions]]. Suppose constants $C\ge0$ and $\rho>1$ satisfy $\|b_\ell\|_{L^2(S^2)}\le C\rho^{-\ell}$ for all $\ell$. Then $b(\omega):=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty b_\ell(\omega)$ converges uniformly on $S^2$, and for every integer $L\ge0$,
$$\sup_{\omega\in S^2}\left|b(\omega)-\sum_{\ell=0}^L b_\ell(\omega)\right|\le C\sqrt{\frac{2L+3}{4\pi}}\,\frac{\rho^{-(L+1)}}{(1-\rho^{-1})^2}.$$
This is a conditional angular-coefficient bound; it does not assert exponential decay for general scattering data.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried from the complete-harmonic supplier used for the addition-kernel estimate. The exponential coefficient hypothesis is explicit and is not deduced for arbitrary contrasts.

items.title: The volume integral scattering operator is compact
items.statement:
Assume AC and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. Then $K_k:L^2(D;\mathbb C)\to L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ is compact and
$$\|K_k\|\le\|G_k(x-y)q(y)\|_{L^2(D\times D)}\le\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{\frac{|D|\operatorname{diam}(D)}{4\pi}}.$$

The proof supplies both the finite-measure Hilbert–Schmidt rescaling route required by the kernel interface and the singular-truncation/Schur route specified for this volume kernel. No uniqueness or outgoing-scattering solvability is asserted here.
items.axiom_use: AC is used by the probability-space square-integrable-kernel supplier and supplies Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for L2 completeness, norm-closure, and Arzelà–Ascoli. The Schur small-ball estimate itself is choice-free once the stated polar-coordinate interface is available.

items.title: Born truncation error for a small-norm volume integral operator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. If $\rho:=\|K_k\|_{L^2\to L^2}<1$, then for every $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ the equation $u=f+K_ku$ has a unique solution. For each integer $m\ge0$, define the Born partial sum $u_m:=\sum_{j=0}^{m}K_k^jf$. Then
$$\|u-u_m\|_2\le\frac{\rho^{m+1}}{1-\rho}\|f\|_2.$$
No compactness, analytic continuation, or physical uniqueness hypothesis is used in this small-norm branch.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used only for completeness of the complex L2 space and the completed-product operator interface; no full Axiom of Choice or Fredholm uniqueness result is used.

references.locator: PDF pp. 80–81, Lippmann–Schwinger volume equation; the small-norm Born estimate is proved locally.

items.title: Cell-volume product integration for the scattering kernel
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D,q,k$ be as in [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]], let $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, and assume $0<|D|<\infty$. Let $P_N$ be the dyadic cell-average projection of [[lem-dyadic-cell-average-projections-converge-in-l2]], and put $K_N:=P_NK_k$ and $f_N:=P_Nf$. This is a finite-rank volume product-integration rule on $L^2(D)$; the projection and kernel convention are fixed by those definitions.

For each positive-measure cell $E_{N,j}$ set $\phi_{N,j}:=|E_{N,j}|^{-1/2}\mathbf1_{E_{N,j}}$. The exact product-cell weights and right-hand side are
$$A^{(N)}_{ij}:=\langle K_k\phi_{N,j},\phi_{N,i}\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|E_{N,i}||E_{N,j}|}}\int_{E_{N,i}}\int_{E_{N,j}}G_k(x-y)q(y)\,dy\,dx,\qquad b^{(N)}_i:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|E_{N,i}|}}\int_{E_{N,i}}f(x)\,dx.$$
For each cell pair, the double integral is absolutely convergent: the kernel $G_k(x-y)q(y)$ is in $L^2(D\times D)$ and $\phi_{N,i}(x)\phi_{N,j}(y)$ has product $L^2$ norm one, so Cauchy--Schwarz makes their product integrable. Completed-product Fubini under Countable Choice then gives the displayed equality with the inner product.
The finite system is $(I-A^{(N)})c=b^{(N)}$, and its reconstruction is $u_N=\sum_jc_j\phi_{N,j}$. Equivalently, it solves $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$ in $V_N$. Its far-field output is the exact cell integral
$$\mathcal F_N(c)(\theta):=\mathcal F_k[u_N](\theta)=\sum_j\frac{c_j}{4\pi\sqrt{|E_{N,j}|}}\int_{E_{N,j}}e^{-ik\theta\cdot y}q(y)\,dy.$$
A singular finite matrix has status `singular`; the definition makes no unconditional invertibility claim. The double integrals are taken over whole cell pairs, including diagonal pairs; no point value of $G_k$ at its singular diagonal is sampled. Finiteness is established by [[lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded]] and [[lem-volume-far-field-map-is-bounded]].

The rule uses exact cell weights as a mathematical discretization. This definition makes no claim about floating-point evaluation or approximate cell weights.
items.axiom_use: The rule is definitional. Its matrix coefficients are finite by the cited kernel-integrability supplier.

items.title: Fredholm solvability and residual stability for volume scattering
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. If $K_k$ is injective through $I-K_k$, then for every $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ there is a unique $u\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ solving $(I-K_k)u=f$, and $A_k:=I-K_k$ has a bounded inverse. Writing $R_k:=\|A_k^{-1}\|$, every $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ satisfies
$$\|u-v\|_2\le R_k\|f-(I-K_k)v\|_2.$$
This is an operator-theoretic Fredholm branch; no physical uniqueness statement for the exterior PDE is asserted.
items.axiom_use: AC is required by the published Fredholm alternative and supplies Countable Choice for completeness of L2(D). The theorem assumes injectivity; it does not prove outgoing-PDE uniqueness for arbitrary contrasts.

references.locator: Printed pp. 60–65, Fredholm solvability and solution error for compact integral operators.

references.locator: Printed pp. 12–13, Fredholm alternative and collectively compact solution stability.

items.title: Radial volume scattering separates into matched partial-wave boundary problems
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $R>0$, $k>0$, and $Q\in C([0,R];\mathbb C)$. Set $q(x)=Q(|x|)$ on $B_R$ and $q(x)=0$ outside $B_R$. Choose for every $\ell$ an orthonormal basis $Y_{\ell m}$ of $\mathcal H_\ell$. Suppose $u^{\rm inc}$ is a classical free Helmholtz field on all of $\mathbb R^3$, and $u=u^{\rm inc}+V$ satisfies the volume-potential equation $V(x)=\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)q(y)u(y)dy$. Assume $u$ is continuous on $\overline B_R$, piecewise $C^2$ on either side of $|x|=R$, and $u$ and its radial derivative are continuous across that interface. For every spherical harmonic $Y_{\ell m}$ assume its coefficient
$$w_{\ell m}(r):=r\int_{S^2}u(r\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\omega)}d\sigma(\omega)$$
satisfies the regular-origin condition $w_{\ell m}(r)=O(r^{\ell+1})$ as $r\downarrow0$. Explicitly assume the incident regular-mode form: for every $\ell,m$ there is $\alpha_{\ell m}\in\mathbb C$ such that $r\int_{S^2}u^{\rm inc}(r\omega)\overline{Y_{\ell m}(\omega)}d\sigma(\omega)=\alpha_{\ell m}rj_\ell(kr)$ for $r>0$. The outgoing radiation condition is $\lim_{r\to\infty}\sup_{\omega\in S^2}|r(\partial_rV(r\omega)-ikV(r\omega))|=0$. Then each reduced mode satisfies
$$w_{\ell m}''(r)+\left(k^2+Q(r)-\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}\right)w_{\ell m}(r)=0\quad(0<r<R),$$
is regular at $0$, and has for $r>R$ the form
$$w_{\ell m}(r)=\alpha_{\ell m}rj_\ell(kr)+\beta_{\ell m}rh_\ell^{(1)}(kr).$$
The interior and exterior values and first derivatives agree at $R$. This is a conditional mode reduction and matching statement; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of the total field.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are inherited from the stated complete-harmonic supplier. The mode equations are finite integrations; no uniqueness of the full scattering problem is inferred.

references.locator: PDF pp. 147–153, radial equation, regular-origin solution, and square-well matching.

items.title: Fredholm convergence and far-field error for cell-volume product integration
items.statement:
Assume AC and the data of [[def-volume-integral-scattering-model]] with $0<|D|<\infty$. Let $f\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$, let $P_N,K_N=P_NK_k,f_N=P_Nf$ and the exact cell-pair matrices be as in [[def-volume-product-integration-scheme]], and suppose $I-K_k$ is injective. Then there is $N_0$ such that for all $N\ge N_0$ the matrix $I-A^{(N)}$ is nonsingular and its reconstruction $u_N\in V_N$ is the unique solution of $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$. If $u\in L^2(D;\mathbb C)$ solves $(I-K_k)u=f$, then for a constant $C<\infty$ independent of $N$ and $f$,
$$\|u_N-u\|_2\le C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr).$$
Writing $C_F:=\|q\|_\infty\sqrt{|D|}/(4\pi)$, the exact far-field outputs obey
$$\|\mathcal F_k[u_N]-\mathcal F_k[u]\|_{C(S^2)}\le C_F C\bigl(\|(P_N-I)K_ku\|_2+\|(P_N-I)f\|_2\bigr)\longrightarrow0.$$
This gives eventual solvability and convergence for the stated cell-volume product rule; it does not assert operator-norm convergence $K_N\to K_k$ or finite-precision error bounds.
items.axiom_use: AC is used for L2 completeness, compact-metric sequential arguments, and the actual collectively compact stability theorem. The projection convergence and finite matrix representation are otherwise explicit.

references.title: Andreas Neubauer and Ronny Ramlau, Lecture Notes: Integral Equations and Boundary Value Problems, §3.3
references.locator: Printed pp. 60–65, collectively compact stability and Nyström solution error. Their specific quadrature rule is on C([0,1]); this theorem separately verifies every generic hypothesis for the L2 volume projections.

references.title: Habib Ammari, Brian Fitzpatrick, and Sanghyeon Yu, Mathematical and Computational Methods in Photonics: Tutorial Notes, §1.3
references.locator: Printed pp. 12–13, generic collectively compact Fredholm solution-stability framework.

title: Volume integral scattering and partial wave error — Examples

items.title: A fixed partial-wave cutoff misses the forward high-frequency plane wave
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For a fixed direction $d\in S^2$, consider the incident plane wave $g_k(\omega)=e^{ikd\cdot\omega}$ on the unit sphere. Let $\Pi_L$ denote projection onto degrees $0,\ldots,L$. For each fixed $L$, its value at the forward direction tends to zero as $k\to\infty$, whereas $g_k(d)=e^{ik}$ has modulus one. Thus a fixed angular cutoff has forward error tending to one; uniform high-frequency accuracy below one requires the cutoff to tend to infinity.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried from the harmonic supplier used for the projection kernel; the decay bound itself is finite integration by parts.

references.title: Pierre Capel, Introduction to Scattering Theory, TALENT lecture notes
references.locator: PDF pp. 17–21, plane-wave partial-wave decomposition; the fixed-cutoff forward-error conclusion is proved locally.

references.title: Maximilian Kreuzer, Quantum Theory: Lecture Notes, version July 15, 2009, Chapter 8
references.locator: PDF pp. 145–150, plane-wave expansion and spherical-harmonic addition identity.

items.title: A small-norm ball scatterer has a certified Born tail
items.statement: Take $D=B(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^3$, constant contrast $q=1/2$, real $k$, and arbitrary $f\in L^2(D)$. The general kernel estimate gives $\|K_k\|\le1/\sqrt6<1$, so the Born series converges and its $m$th partial sum has an explicit geometric error bound.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Born theorem for L2 completeness; the numerical norm bound itself is a direct kernel estimate.

references.title: Otmar Scherzer and Leonidas Mindrinos, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Sommersemester 2015, Chapter 5, §5.2.6
references.locator: PDF pp. 79–82, Lippmann–Schwinger volume equation; the ball norm and geometric Born tail are calculated locally.

references.title: Habib Ammari, Brian Fitzpatrick, and Sanghyeon Yu, Mathematical and Computational Methods in Photonics: Tutorial Notes, §1.3
references.locator: Printed pp. 11–12, Neumann-series solution estimate.

items.title: A near-unit volume-operator mode amplifies forcing error
items.statement: Conditionally suppose a compact volume operator $K_k$ has a normalized eigenmode $\phi$ with eigenvalue $\lambda\ne1$, and suppose $I-K_k$ is injective. The Fredholm branch then applies. Forcing along $\phi$ is amplified by exactly $|1-\lambda|^{-1}$; this example does not claim that every physical contrast has such an eigenvalue.
items.axiom_use: The operator-theoretic existence and residual estimate inherit the Axiom of Choice from the Fredholm theorem; the eigenvector calculation is algebraic.

references.title: Andreas Neubauer and Ronny Ramlau, Lecture Notes: Integral Equations and Boundary Value Problems, §3.3
references.locator: Printed pp. 60–65, Fredholm solvability and solution-error conditioning.

references.title: Habib Ammari, Brian Fitzpatrick, and Sanghyeon Yu, Mathematical and Computational Methods in Photonics: Tutorial Notes, §1.3
references.locator: Printed pp. 12–13, compact Fredholm stability and inverse-norm amplification.

items.title: Exact matching for the radial square well in the zeroth partial wave
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $Q(r)=V_0>0$ on $0\le r\le R$, let $k>0$, and put $\kappa=\sqrt{k^2+V_0}$. In the $\ell=0$ reduced radial channel with incident regular mode $w^{\rm inc}(r)=\sin(kr)/k$, write the regular interior solution as $A\sin(\kappa r)$ and the exterior total mode as $\sin(kr)/k+B e^{ikr}$. Exact continuity of the value and derivative determines $A$ and $B$ below.
items.axiom_use: No additional axiom is used; the example is a two-equation boundary matching calculation under the radial theorem's conditional hypotheses.

references.title: Maximilian Kreuzer, Quantum Theory: Lecture Notes, version July 15, 2009, Chapter 8
references.locator: PDF pp. 151–153, exact radial square-well matching.

references.title: Pierre Capel, Introduction to Scattering Theory, TALENT lecture notes
references.locator: PDF pp. 29–32, radial matching and phase-shift conventions.
